name: Bearish Double Vertical (Put Debit + Call Credit)
summary: Buy a put debit spread financed by selling a call credit spread in the same expiry - the bearish mirror of the bullish double vertical.

legs.strike_rule: short call strike plus width Wc
long put strike minus width Wp, placed at the downside target

max_profit: (Wp - net debit) x 100 (or Wp + net credit) below the short put strike
max_loss: (Wc + net debit) x 100 (or Wc - net credit) above the long call strike
breakevens: upper breakeven within the call spread and lower breakeven at long put strike - net debit; compute both numerically at entry and store them

greeks.theta: slightly positive when the call credit spread dominates

when_to_use: Directionally bearish with IV rank >= 25 and a defined downside target. Call-side skew is usually cheaper than put-side skew, so this structure finances less well than its bullish twin - demand a better entry price.
entry_rules: Bearish trigger required: price below the 50-day SMA AND 20-day SMA slope negative, or a breakdown below the 20-day low
Short call at 0.20-0.25 delta; short put at the downside target (measured move or 20-day ATR x 2 below spot)
DTE 30-60, no earnings inside the expiry
OI >= 500 and spread <= 10% of mid on all four legs
management_rules: Take profit at 60% of max profit
Close the call credit spread at 50% of its credit if the put spread is still working
Loss stop at 1.0x the put spread's max profit
Trend invalidation: close if price closes above the 50-day SMA
exit_rules: Force-close by 15:45 ET on expiration day, always
Close the call vertical immediately if the short call goes ITM by more than 0.25 x Wc, its delta >= 0.85, or its extrinsic < $0.10

Ex-dividend guard on the short call - close before the ex-date if extrinsic < the projected dividend (short calls are assigned for dividends, and in a bearish trade the call side is the losing side, making this doubly likely)
Close the put vertical when the short put goes ITM and its extrinsic < $0.10 (max profit region)
assignment_risk: The short call is the live risk in a rally (delivers 100 SHORT shares per contract, plus dividend liability if held over an ex-date). The short put only matters at max profit.
buying_power: Max of the two verticals' requirements, typically (Wc - call credit) x 100 per contract plus any net debit.
common_mistakes: Selling the call spread too close in a squeeze; ignoring dividend assignment on the short call; assuming the financing quality matches the bullish version.
zero_dte_notes: Same intraday handling as the bullish version, mirrored. Short call assignment is not a dividend concern on 0DTE but deep ITM short calls still get exercised at expiry - force-close at 15:45 ET.
family: four-leg structures (iron condors, iron butterflies, condors, double calendars/diagonals, boxes, jelly rolls, conversions/reversals, double verticals, double ratio spreads)
